newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins edge up on U.S. employment data.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins edge up on U.S. employment data.

text.p: Russian MinFins edged up on Tuesday, as investors found the U.S. fourth quarter employment cost index to their liking, dealers said.
"The figures were positive for the market," said Pavel Sool, chief dealer at Sberbank. "Bids are firm and demand obviously prevails."
The U.S. Labor Department reported that its employment cost index rose 0.8 percent in the fourth quarter against a 0.6 percent gain in the third quarter.

A trader at International Moscow Bank said the market sank in the morning, with the biggest selling in the fourth and fifth tranches. But he said that after the U.S. figures were released, investors started buying all tranches.
Sool forecast a stable market until February on positive news about President Boris Yeltsin's health.
Foreign debt restructuring and progress in talks with the International Monetary Fund about a new tranche of its $10 billion loan to Russia could also boost the market, he said.
Plakhotny said news that Yeltsin had worked at the Kremlin for three hours on Tuesday elicited no reaction from the market.
"The market is tired," he said. "Such news can no longer cause any reaction. We need something more serious to react."
Dealers had not yet seen Yeltsin's televised Kremlin appearance, which showed the president, who is recovering from pneumonia, looking alert in the first new pictures of him since January 6.
They said MinFins were unlikely to fall, since Russian paper was considered cheap.
"The support is good at current levels and we shall fluctuate in this range until February at least," one dealer said.
